skills.name: Pressure: definition, calculation and units; pressure in solids

note.text:
Pressure is the force acting normally (at right angles) on unit area: P = F ÷ A.
• Unit: the pascal, 1 Pa = 1 N/m². Also N/cm² and kPa (1 kPa = 1000 Pa).
• The same force on a smaller area gives a larger pressure; on a larger area, a smaller pressure.
• Applications: knives and needles are sharp (small area, high pressure); lorries have many wide tyres, tractors have wide tracks, and building foundations are wide (large area, low pressure).
• Change cm² to m² by dividing by 10 000.

sections.heading: Force and area
sections.text:
Push a drawing pin into a board: the sharp point goes in easily, but the flat head would not. The force is the same; what changes is the area.
Pressure measures how concentrated a force is: P = F ÷ A, where F is the force acting at right angles to the surface and A is the area.
The unit is the pascal: {1} Pa = {1} N/m². Pressures are often large, so kPa ({1000} Pa) is also used.

sections.heading: Small area, large pressure
sections.text:
• Knives, axes, needles and nails have thin edges or points: tiny area, huge pressure, so they cut or pierce easily.
• Football boots have studs to grip the ground.
• A woman's narrow heel can damage a soft floor because her weight acts on a tiny area.

sections.heading: Large area, small pressure
sections.text:
• Lorries have many wide tyres; tractors and bulldozers have wide tracks, so they do not sink into mud.
• Buildings stand on wide foundations so the soil is not overloaded.
• Carrying a load on a flat pad on the head is more comfortable than on a narrow strap.
Remember to change cm² to m² (divide by {10000}) before working out pascals.

key_words.meaning: force per unit area, P = F ÷ A
a force at right angles to a surface

mistake.why: The pascal is N per square metre: change cm² to m² first.

worked_example.problem: A man weighing {F} N stands on both feet. The total area of his soles is {A} m². Find the pressure on the floor.

cards.idea: A smaller area gives a bigger pressure for the same force.
example: A sharp knife cuts because its edge has a tiny area.

cards.idea: Change cm² to m²: divide by {10000}.

check.prompt: A woman of weight {W} N stands on one heel of area {a} cm². Find the pressure on the floor (Pa).

misconceptions.explain: That is in N/cm². Change cm² to m² first (÷ {10000}).
Divide the force by the area.

questions.prompt: A force of {F} N acts on an area of {A} m². Find the pressure (Pa).

misconceptions.explain: Pressure is force divided by area.
Force on top, area underneath: P = F ÷ A.

pick.q: Why is a kitchen knife sharpened?
pick.r: A thin edge has a small area, so the pressure is large
w: A thin edge has a large area
Sharpening reduces the force needed to lift it
e: A thin edge has a small area.
Sharpening removes metal; it is lighter.
Lifting has nothing to do with cutting.
pick.y: The same push over a smaller area gives a bigger pressure.

pick.q: Why do heavy lorries have many wide tyres?
pick.r: To spread the weight over a large area and reduce the pressure on the road
w: To increase the pressure on the road
To make the lorry go faster
To reduce the weight of the lorry
e: Large pressure would damage the road and sink into soft ground.
Tyre width is about pressure, not speed.
pick.y: A large area reduces the pressure.

pick.q: Why are the foundations of a building made wide?
pick.r: To reduce the pressure on the ground so the building does not sink
w: To increase the pressure on the ground
e: High pressure would make the building sink.
Width of the foundation is about pressure on the soil.
pick.y: A wide base spreads the weight over a large area.

questions.prompt: A pressure of {P} Pa acts on an area of {A} m². Find the force (N).
A woman of weight {W} N stands on one heel of area {a} cm². Find the pressure on the floor (Pa).

misconceptions.explain: That is in N/cm². Change cm² to m² first (÷ {10000}).
Divide the force by the area.

questions.prompt: A brick of weight {W} N measures {l} m × {w} m × {h} m. What is the greatest pressure it can exert when standing on a table (Pa)?

misconceptions.explain: That is the pressure on the largest face, the smallest pressure. Use the smallest area for the greatest pressure.

solution: The greatest pressure is on the smallest face: {w} m × {h} m = {roundTo(w * h, 0.0001)} m².
